title: Our Little Bark, on Boisterous Seas
description: Our Little Bark, on Boisterous Seas in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 830 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Thanksgiving for Deliverance in a Storm”, where the book credits them to Madan's Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our lit-tle bark, on bois-terous seas, By cru-el tem-pests tossed, With-out one cheer-ful beam of hope, Ex-pect-ing to be lost,

lines: Our little bark, on boisterous seas,
Without one cheerful beam of hope,
We to the Lord, in humble prayer,
Though feeble, yet with contrite hearts,
Then ceased the stormy winds to blow;
And soon again a placid sea
O, may our grateful, trembling hearts
To him who hath our lives preserved, —

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
